data.claim: After the operator answers the canonical ddflow approvals ask payload in the Kilo question tool, one call to H.attest_pending attests every pending request whose canonical question has an accepted answer, recording it approved at level 2 (via=harness), spendable with no terminal approve.
data.falsifier: A pending request whose Kilo question part uses a NON-canonical question text is not matched by scan_kilo and stays pending.
data.mechanism: attest_pending iterates E.pending(state) and calls attest for each; attest's find() calls scan_kilo() matching the Kilo question part on question == row['text'] (the canonical ask text) and the ask id marker, then E.answer records the outcome.

chunk_findings.detail: The new loop delegates to the existing `attest`, but no part of this change updates the ask/question channel to surface the canonical ask payload. Per B3068414423, `attest` matching is keyed to the canonical payload while the operator’s real chat answer is keyed to the currently surfaced non-canonical text. In the real existing ask flow, `attest` returns `(False, non-WAITING)` for an answered request and `approvals_attest_all` therefore attests nothing. A regression test that writes the transcript answer directly against the canonical payload can pass while the operator-facing flow still fails.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/harness.py:attest_pending

chunk_findings.detail: The function computes `refused`, but the `if attested:` branch is checked first and returns `O.ok` before `if refused:` can run. Concretely, with two pending requests A and B, where A has an accepted answer and B has an answered-but-refused/invalid transcript, `attest_pending` returns A `ok=True` and B `ok=False`. Since `attested` is truthy, the function returns `O.ok` containing only A’s message; B’s refusal is dropped, the CLI exits success, and B remains pending silently. Mixed success/refusal should not report an overall success.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/approvals_harness.py:approvals_attest_all

chunk_findings.detail: The patch adds only a manual `ddflow approvals attest --all` CLI branch and an API function; there is no code path in the change that invokes `approvals_attest_all` after the operator answers in chat. The operator must still open a terminal and run this command after answering, so the stated goal that “a chat answer alone approves with no terminal/SSH” is not met, and the missing auto-attest loop from B3068414423 remains unresolved.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/commands/approvals.py:cmd_approvals_attest

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test never drives the production surfaced-question path that B3068414423 says is broken. It writes `_kilo_question(row["text"], yes)` directly, using the canonical ask stored on the event row, and never asks the changed `ddflow/surfaces/declared/approvals.py` what text was actually shown to the operator in Kilo. An implementation could add `H.attest_pending` while still surfacing the old non-canonical ask, and this test would pass because it sidesteps the mismatch. The actual bug sequence—operator answers the surfaced non-canonical text—is not covered.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_approvals_harness.py::test_an_answer_in_kilo_to_the_canonical_ask_is_auto_attested_to_approved

chunk_findings.detail: `approvals_attest_all` treats any successful attest as the whole batch: if one pending id attests and another comes back not-ok with a message that does not start with `H.WAITING`, the function still returns `O.ok` and joins only the `ok` messages, dropping the refusal. Given pending requests A (transcript answer that `attest` accepts) and B (answer `attest` refuses, for example a digest or label mismatch), `--all` exits success and B’s refusal never appears in the outcome, so the caller can treat the batch as approved while B stays pending.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/approvals_harness.py:approvals_attest_all

chunk_findings.detail: The change makes the positional `id` optional even when `--all` is not supplied. Given input `ddflow approvals attest` with no id and no `--all`, the parser now accepts the invocation and calls `AH.approvals_attest(c.repo, a.id, ...)` with `a.id == ""`. Previously this was rejected as a missing required argument. The empty string is not a valid request id, so the command now attempts to attest request `""` instead of producing a usage error.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/approvals.py:Param("id", positional=True, nargs="?", default="")

chunk_findings.detail: The test never creates a refused request. `t3` is only filed with no corresponding transcript answer, so `attest_pending` reports it as unanswered/`WAITING`, not as an answered-but-refused or invalid transcript. The fixed `refused` branch from the confirmed prior defect is therefore not exercised: for a correct `approvals_attest_all`, `refused` remains empty and the one attested request makes the function return success, causing the test’s `assert code == 3` to fail against the intended fix. If the implementation instead classifies `WAITING` as `refused` to make this pass, it contradicts the separate no-answer semantics in `test_auto_attest_leaves_a_request_without_an_answer_pending`. The test needs a real invalid/refused transcript for `t3`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_approvals_harness.py:test_attest_all_reports_a_refused_request_beside_an_attested_one

chunk_findings.detail: Making `id` optional (`nargs="?"`, `default=""`) without requiring exactly one of `id` or `--all` means `ddflow approvals attest` (no id, no `--all`) no longer fails at parse time. `a.all` is false, so the function calls `approvals_attest` with `a.id == ""`. That is not a request id, so the call cannot attest anything and the operator gets a domain refusal/lookup failure instead of a usage error; `--all` and a positional id are also unordered, so a bare attest is now a silent mis-dispatch of the path this change added.

chunk_findings.detail: The new auto-attest path only re-runs `attest(log, cfg, row["id"], ...)` over `E.pending`. For the bug’s actual input — the Kilo question tool surfaced non-canonical question text — the transcript does not contain the canonical ask payload, so `attest` returns the WAITING message, `approvals_attest_all` falls through to the `O.nothing` branch, and the request stays pending. The diff never edits the ask surface or scan/payload matching, so `ddflow approvals attest --all` still does not approve the chat answer and B3068414423 remains.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/harness.py:attest_pending

chunk_findings.detail: With one answered pending request and one unanswered pending request, `results` contains one `ok: True` row and one `ok: False` row whose message starts with `H.WAITING`. `refused` is empty and `attested` is non-empty, so the function returns `O.ok` with `lines` containing only the ok result. The WAITING result is omitted from the outcome and the exit status is success. `ddflow approvals attest --all` then tells the caller the batch succeeded while an unanswered approval remains pending.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/approvals_harness.py:approvals_attest_all

chunk_findings.detail: Prior finding #3 still holds for the `--all` plus positional `id` case: `if a.all:` is checked first and `a.id` is never examined. `ddflow approvals attest --all req-123` silently ignores `req-123` and attests every answered pending request; the new refusal only handles the missing-id case, not the conflicting-arguments case.

chunk_findings.detail: The test is named and documented as verifying that `attest --all` reports a refused request beside an **attested** one, but its final assertion only checks `asks_of(fold(...))[row["id"]]["state"] == "answered"`. That state can be present even when the answered T2 request was never actually auto-attested: an implementation that records/reports the T3 refusal (`code == 3`, `"refused" in err`) but fails to write a harness attest event for `row` still leaves the test passing. It should additionally assert that `row` has `outcome == "approved"` and `via == "harness"` (as the direct auto-attest test does) in this mixed path.

chunk_findings.detail: In the mixed-result branch, the code returns `O.refused(..., id=attested, refused=[...])`, where `attested` is the list of IDs that **succeeded**. Given input with two pending approvals where `A` attests successfully and `B` is refused, downstream consumers that read the standard `outcome.id` field on a refused outcome will see `["A"]` (the request that actually succeeded) and not `["B"]` (the request that was refused). The refused IDs are only carried separately in `outcome.refused`; putting the successful IDs in `id` makes the refused outcome identify the wrong request.

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test does not exercise the actual “operator answers the Kilo question tool” path that B3068414423 is about: it manually writes `row["text"]` into the Kilo DB and then directly calls `H.attest_pending(log, cfg)`. A broken patch that still never auto-attests after the operator answers through the chat surface—while merely adding an `attest_pending` function—would make this test pass, leaving the reported bug in place. The CLI tests similarly invoke `ddflow approvals attest --all` explicitly, so none of the added tests verify that a chat answer alone triggers attestation without a terminal command.
